title: Voices in the wall
steps: The room lit at last; a crack in the right wall; voices beyond it. The three of you creep over to it and stay very still.

A cold voice that seems to come from the stone itself whispers: *tomorrow's flying lesson, the brooms in the shed, the words to say to each broom; after that, no one will make the boy fly for a long while*.
An older pupil's voice answers, afraid: *what if someone gets hurt?* And the cold voice: *a fright, no more; and a lesson for those who think the castle is theirs*. Then steps going away.
That was a pupil, and the other voice was no pupil's: it came from the wall!
Someone is going to tamper with the brooms for tomorrow's lesson, and we cannot tell anyone without confessing we were out of bed.
Then we stop it ourselves, tomorrow, before the lesson. But first, back to bed without Dask seeing us.
The way home: you walk back to the door and go down through it, down the corridor beyond, into the dark of the way down.
